experiences.title: Fetch-execute factory
experiences.description: Step inside the CPU and follow an instruction through the fetch-decode-execute cycle. Includes a 3D CPU you can take apart.

experiences.title: Von Neumann HQ
experiences.description: Meet John von Neumann and explore the stored-program architecture inside nearly every computer. Includes a 3D model of the architecture.

experiences.title: Speed lab
experiences.description: Find out how clock speed, cache size and number of cores affect CPU performance. Includes a 3D multi-core CPU and a motherboard with cooling.

experiences.title: Smart home
experiences.description: Find the embedded systems hidden around a smart home, and take apart a 3D washing machine to see the computer inside.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 1.1 test is done on paper. Revisit the lessons you found hardest first, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Types of network: zoom out
experiences.description: Zoom out from one computer to a school LAN and the whole world. Standalone computers, LANs and WANs.

experiences.title: Network control room
experiences.description: Take charge of a slow school network and find the five factors that affect performance.

experiences.title: Network showdown
experiences.description: Client-server takes on peer-to-peer. Find out who does what in each model, then settle the torrent debate.

experiences.title: Mission: wire up the school
experiences.description: Explore a school server room and find the hardware that connects a LAN.

experiences.title: Inside the internet
experiences.description: Find out what the internet really is, how DNS finds websites, and what hosting and the cloud mean.

experiences.title: Star and mesh networks
experiences.description: Break a star network, then see how full, partial and wireless mesh networks compare.

experiences.title: Revision HQ
experiences.description: Recap lessons 1 to 6 and find out what to revise before your mid-topic test.

experiences.title: Assessment 1
experiences.description: Your 1.3 test on lessons 1 to 7 is done on paper. Warm up first with Revision HQ, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Connection café
experiences.description: Ethernet, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth? Compare wired and wireless connections and recommend the right one for each job.

experiences.title: Cipher room
experiences.description: Crack a cipher, learn how keys work, and find out how Wi-Fi keeps your data secret with WPA2.

experiences.title: Address sorting office
experiences.description: Sort MAC, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and find out why the world needed IPv6.

experiences.title: Protocol city
experiences.description: Explore the standards and protocols that make networks work, from HTTP to TCP/IP.

experiences.title: Layer burger bar
experiences.description: Build networking in layers, like a burger, and find out why layering protocols makes networks easier to build.

experiences.title: Revision HQ 2
experiences.description: Recap lessons 9 to 13 and find out what to revise before your end-of-unit assessment.

experiences.title: Assessment 2 reflection
experiences.description: Once your end-of-unit test is marked, use this sheet to plan what to improve.

experiences.title: Threat map
experiences.description: Meet the six forms of attack on the OCR specification, find out why attackers do it, and follow the CryptoLocker story.

experiences.title: Malware lab
experiences.description: Study viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware and spyware under the microscope, and learn how to stop them.

experiences.title: Database break-in
experiences.description: See how a single quotation mark in a login box can hand over a database, and learn how programmers stop it.

experiences.title: Phishing inbox
experiences.description: Work through a suspicious inbox: learn what phishing is, what attackers gain, and how to spot the signs.

experiences.title: Social engineering HQ
experiences.description: People are the weakest link: blagging, shouldering, baiting and the everyday habits that let attackers in.

experiences.title: Cracking lab
experiences.description: See how fast a computer can guess passwords, and learn what makes a password, and a login page, hard to crack.

experiences.title: Traffic flood
experiences.description: Watch a website drown under fake traffic: DoS, DDoS, botnets and zombies, and the day half the internet went down.

experiences.title: Packet sniffers
experiences.description: Data can be read as it travels. Learn how interception works, what it gives attackers, and how encryption stops it.

experiences.title: Defence depot
experiences.description: The first four prevention methods: penetration testing, anti-malware, firewalls and user access levels.

experiences.title: Defence depot 2
experiences.description: Passwords, encryption and physical security, and choosing the right defence for each threat.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 1.4 test is done on paper. Warm up with the Cyber defence game, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Cyber defence
experiences.description: Spend a budget on protections, identify each incoming threat and find out whether your defences hold. Three lives, then the network shuts down.

experiences.title: Security desk
experiences.description: Check every sign-up at the security desk: learn the validation checks that stop bad data getting in.

experiences.title: Cyber defence HQ
experiences.description: Defend a program against misuse, bots and weak passwords with authentication and defensive design.

experiences.title: Code clinic
experiences.description: Diagnose unreadable code, learn the habits that make programs maintainable, and refine an algorithm to make it robust.

experiences.title: Bug hunt lab
experiences.description: Find out why and when programs are tested, and learn to tell syntax errors from logic errors.

experiences.title: Test lab
experiences.description: Choose normal, boundary, invalid and erroneous test data, and build a test table that really tests a program.

experiences.title: Revision HQ 2.3
experiences.description: Recap lessons 1 to 5 of Producing robust programs and find out what to revise before your test.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 2.3 test is done on paper. Warm up first with Revision HQ 2.3, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Logic gate lab
experiences.description: Meet AND, OR and NOT, fill in their truth tables, then build your own logic circuits by dragging gates and wires.

experiences.title: Truth table detectives
experiences.description: Crack two- and three-input truth tables, including intermediate columns, and work out logic from electric circuits.

experiences.title: Circuit workshop
experiences.description: Turn real scenarios into logic circuits and truth tables: an alarm, a police cell and a factory's emergency override.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 2.4 test is done on paper. Warm up with Logic sprint first, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Logic sprint
experiences.description: Two minutes, random circuits and expressions, speed bonuses and streaks. Replay as often as you like to beat your personal best.
